confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from three web searches. Beer and cappuccino come from crowd-sourced MyLifeElsewhere/Numbeo-style data (about RON 15 each, roughly $3.4). Restaurant meals come from Wise, Traveltables (2023) and OkVoyage figures, which range from about $7.5 to $13 for an inexpensive meal and about $37 to $64 for a mid-range meal for two. I used a bounded middle value and adjusted for inflation. I found no direct cocktail or wine-by-the-glass prices, so cocktail is about twice the local beer price and wine glass is about 1.2 times the beer price, which is a weak basis. The RBA rate is the 18 November 2026 observation seen in search results for the RBA's exchange-rate pages. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge of Cluj-Napoca (a university and tech city with strong event and festival demand). I did not search for or inspect any accommodation listings, so these are the least certain anchors.
comparable_city_reasoning: Cluj-Napoca is Romania's second-largest city and more expensive than the national average. Restaurants run about 20% above the national level per MyLifeElsewhere. I treated it as comparable to other mid-priced Central and Eastern European university and tourism cities such as Brasov, Sibiu, Krakow and Budapest, at the lower end of that group.
